definitions: being, relating to, or belonging to a person or to people as opposed to animals :
having the qualities , faults , and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods , animals , or machines :
belonging to the genus (= group of species ) Homo :
a person :
a member of a species of the genus (= group of species ) Homo :
examples: The human body is composed of about 60 percent water .
Police searching for the missing woman found human remains in woodland .
Victory in the war was achieved at the cost of great human suffering .
The inspector declared the meat fit for human consumption (= in good enough condition for people to eat )
Of course I make mistakes , I'm only human.
When he laughs it makes him seem more human.

definitions: ( especially of things that are not living ) being a large distance from top to bottom or a long way above the ground , or having the stated distance from top to bottom :
greater than the usual level or amount :
containing a large quantity of something:
very good or very moral standards :
fast , strong wind :
examples: a high building / mountain
high ceilings
It's two and a half metres high and one metre wide .
The corn grew waist-high (= as high as a person's waist )
The job demands a high level of concentration .
He suffers from high blood pressure .

definitions: present participle of have
physical or other injury or damage :
to hurt someone or damage something:
damage done to something:
used to say that an action is not helpful and could make a situation worse :
to damage something or make something worse :
examples: It was not my intention to cause any harm.
Missing a meal once in a while never did anyone any harm.
A mistake like that will do his credibility a lot of harm.
She was frightened by the experience but she came to no harm (= was not hurt )
Thankfully no one was harmed in the accident .
The government's reputation has already been harmed by a series of scandals .

definitions: to make it possible or easier for someone to do something, by doing part of the work yourself or by providing advice , money , support , etc.:
If something helps a difficult or painful situation , it improves it or makes it easier or less painful :
If something or someone helps to do something, that thing or person is one of several reasons for it happening :
If you can't/couldn't help something, such as acting in a particular way or making a particular remark , you are/were not able to control or stop it:
to give something to someone:
examples: How can I help you?
I wonder if you could help me - I'd like some information about flights to New Zealand.
Nothing can help her now (= her situation is too bad for anyone to be able to improve it)
I feel that learning English will help (= improve )
My dad said he would help with the costs of (= give part of the cost of)
Maybe I can help with planning the party ?

definitions: (the study of or a record of) past events considered together, especially events of a particular period , country , or subject :
something that happened or ended a long time ago and is not important now, or a person who is not important now, although they were in the past:
something that has been done or experienced by a particular person or thing repeatedly over a long period :
(the study of) past events considered together, esp . events or developments of a particular period , country , or subject :
something that has been done or experienced by a particular person or thing many times over a long period :
examples: I studied modern European history at college .
American history
Annie decided to write a history of electronic music .
I only asked him for a cigarette , but two hours later he'd told me his whole life history.
Last year's report is ancient history and totally irrelevant to the current situation .
"What about Dan - are you still seeing him?" "Oh, he's history."

definitions: either of the two equal or nearly equal parts that together make up a whole :
Half past a particular hour is 30 minutes later than that hour :
only partly :
to divide the cost of something with someone:
equal amounts of two different things:
examples: "What's half of 96?" "48."
Roughly half (of) the class are Spanish and the others are a mixture of nationalities .
Cut the apple in half (= into two equal parts )
Cut the larger tomatoes into halves.
The recipe tells you to use a pound and a half of butter .
She was born in the latter half of the 18th century .

definitions: something that you do often and regularly , sometimes without knowing that you are doing it:
something annoying that someone often does:
a strong physical need to keep taking a particular drug :
to stop doing something that you have always done; often used when you are criticizing someone in a humorous way:
a special piece of long clothing worn by monks and nuns
examples: He has an annoying habit of arriving just when we are having our meal .
I always buy the same brand of toothpaste out of (= because of)
I'm trying not to get into (= start )
I used to swim twice a week , but I seem to have got out of (= ended )
I was taught to drive by my boyfriend and I'm afraid I've picked up (= copied )
I'm trying to get him to break (= end intentionally )

definitions: the feeling of being happy :
a phrase used to say that you hope someone will be very happy , especially in a new situation such as a marriage or a new home :
the feeling of being pleased or happy :
examples: It was only later in life that she found happiness and peace of mind .
Will you join me in wishing the bride and groom every happiness?
Our children have brought us so much happiness.

definitions: the organ in your chest that sends the blood around your body :
used to refer to a person's character , or the place within a person where feelings or emotions are considered to come from:
the central or most important part :
the firm central part of a vegetable , especially one with a lot of leaves :
courage , determination , or hope :
examples: He's got a weak / bad heart (= his heart is not healthy )
Isabel's heart was beating fast with fright .
She has a good heart (= she is a kind person )
His heart leaped (= he suddenly felt very excited and happy )
The demonstrators will march through the heart of the capital .
A disagreement about boundaries is at the heart of the dispute .

definitions: (of a situation or an event ) to have existence or come into existence :
If something happens to someone or something, it has an effect on him, her, or it:
to do or be by chance :
perhaps :
(of a situation or event ) to come into existence ; occur :
examples: No one knows exactly what happened but several people have been hurt .
Anything could happen in the next half hour .
A funny thing happened in the office today.
I don't want to think about what might have happened if he'd been driving any faster .
I don't know what I'd do if anything happened to him (= if he was hurt , became ill , or died )
They happened to look (= looked by chance )

an amount of food served to a person at one time :

definitions: buildings for people to live in:
a case or covering that surrounds a machine or part of a machine :
buildings that people live in, or the providing of places for people to live :
buildings for people to live in, used especially when talking about their price or condition :

examples: There's a shortage of cheap housing in the region .

affordable / expensive housing

definitions: very, to a large degree , or at a high level :
in a way that shows admiration and respect :
in an important or influential (= having a lot of influence ) position :
in an important or influential position :
in a position that is important or that has a lot of influence :
examples: She was offered a highly paid job in finance .
a highly profitable line of products

Her colleagues think very highly of her work .
He's very highly thought of within the company .
Many people speak highly of Haines.

definitions: the amount of time during the day or week that you work :
examples: The company have threatened to cut my hours at work .
People in executive roles often work long hours .
reduce/cut/increase sb's hours The company have threatened to cut my hours at work .
long/flexible hours People in executive roles often work long hours .

a huge forest
